title: Kojiki
author: ono-yasumaro
attributionNote: Compiled by Ō no Yasumaro in 712 CE at imperial command, drawing on earlier oral and written traditions. The compiler is historically established; the underlying myths are traditional.
description: Japan's oldest surviving chronicle, in three books: the age of the kami from the first deities through the creation of the islands, the descent of the heavenly grandchild and the founding of the imperial line, and the reigns of the early emperors down to 628 CE. Chamberlain's translation prints the work in 180 numbered sections.
historicalContext: The Kojiki was compiled in the Nara period as part of the state's consolidation of myth, genealogy and legitimacy, and was presented to the court in 712. Long studied as a philological monument of the Japanese language, it became central to Shinto and to later Japanese nationalism.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Wikisource section by section at read time. Chamberlain's 1882 translation is public domain; the classical Japanese and Chinese source text is not included.
